title: Understanding Compound Interest
content: Compound interest is the addition of interest to the principal sum of a loan or deposit, or in other words, interest on interest. It is the result of reinvesting interest, rather than paying it out, so that interest in the next period is then earned on the principal sum plus previously accumulated interest. The key drivers of compounding are time horizon, compounding frequency, and rate of return. Starting to invest early exponentially enhances compounding returns.
